question: A family is overwhelmed with funeral plans and hospital paperwork right after a death. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Tell them to figure it out since the patient is already gone
options.B: Advise them to ignore all paperwork for at least a month
options.C: Guide them step-by-step and connect them with social work
options.D: Take over their personal bank accounts to pay expenses

explanation: You got it! Offering practical guidance and linking them to social services helps lift the heavy load when they are emotionally exhausted.

question: What is the main idea behind person-centered care planning?

options.A: Allowing the nursing staff to make all daily decisions without input
options.B: Focusing solely on medical diagnoses while ignoring social history
options.C: Enforcing a strict morning schedule that all residents must follow
options.D: Tailoring care around the individual preferences and past routines of the resident

explanation: Exactly right! Person-centered care treats the resident as a unique human being, honoring their personal history and everyday preferences.

question: A patient arrives with a massive pulmonary embolism. What is happening in their body?

options.A: Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries is blocked, impairing oxygenation
options.B: The liver has stopped producing clotting factors, causing widespread bleeding
options.C: An infection in the urinary tract has spread into the spinal fluid
options.D: Gastric acid is leaking directly into the peritoneal cavity through an ulcer

explanation: A pulmonary embolism is a blocked blood vessel in the lungs. Because the blockage is there, blood can't pick up fresh oxygen to circulate.

question: You walk into a patient's room and see a big loop of chest tube tubing resting on the floor. What should you do first?

options.A: Clamp the chest tube immediately and page the physician for urgent removal
options.B: Lift the drainage canister up and place it on the patient's bed
options.C: Adjust the tubing so it coils loosely on the bed and drains freely without kinks
options.D: Disconnect the tubing joints to empty the pooled fluid onto the floor

explanation: Spot on! Dependent loops trap fluid and block drainage. Arranging the tubing neatly on the bed lets everything flow smoothly again.

question: What is the main goal when a patient arrives in the emergency department?

options.A: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.B: To discharge patients within a strict time limit
options.C: To complete detailed medical histories for all patients
options.D: To stabilize life-threatening conditions swiftly

explanation: Spot on! In emergency nursing, the absolute priority is making sure the patient stays alive and stable before worrying about anything else. You're doing great!

question: What is the primary goal of long-term care?

options.A: Restricting resident autonomy to maintain strict institutional rules
options.B: Ensuring rapid patient discharge within seventy-two hours
options.C: Completely reversing all chronic disease processes
options.D: Promoting the highest possible level of well-being and independence

explanation: Great thinking! Long-term care isn't about a quick cure; it's about helping residents stay as independent and happy as possible every single day.

question: Which residential model features 24-hour staff presence for high support?

options.A: Self-contained private flats
options.B: Supervised hostels
options.C: Temporary weekend shelters
options.D: Transitional living facilities

explanation: Well done! Supervised hostels have staff around the clock to give extra guidance to residents who still need help with daily routines and medications.

question: What do we call the fraction of a drug that successfully reaches the bloodstream in an active, unchanged form?

options.A: Clearance rate
options.B: Half-life
options.C: Bioavailability
options.D: Volume of distribution

explanation: Bioavailability simply means 'how much active drug is actually available' to your body to do its job after the journey.

question: What happens to the fetal skull bones after the baby is delivered and moulding is no longer needed?

options.A: They remain permanently overlapped until the child reaches toddler age
options.B: They fuse together immediately to protect the brain from outside injury
options.C: They gradually return to their normal shape as the pressure is relieved
options.D: They separate permanently and require surgical correction in the nursery

explanation: Because the skull bones are flexible and joined by elastic tissue, the head regains its normal rounded appearance shortly after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: What is an epithelial tissue made of just a single layer of cells called?

options.A: Stratified epithelium
options.B: Compound epithelium
options.C: Pseudo epithelium
options.D: Simple epithelium

explanation: The word 'simple' here just means 'one layer thick'! This makes it great for letting things pass through easily.

question: A nurse researcher wants to check if there is a link between water source type and the prevalence of cholera in a community. Which study type is best?

options.A: Qualitative interview study
options.B: Analytical cross-sectional study
options.C: Purely descriptive case report
options.D: Longitudinal clinical trial

explanation: When you are looking for a connection between two things at one specific time, an analytical cross-sectional study is your best friend.

question: Why must nurses regularly check the expiration dates of medicines in a clinic pharmacy?

options.A: To decide which nurse gets a promotion
options.B: To prevent patients from receiving expired or ineffective drugs
options.C: To make the medicine shelves look neat and colorful
options.D: To increase the financial profit of the local government

explanation: Expired medications may lose their chemical potency or become toxic, harming the patient instead of curing them. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the main job of a septic tank in an individual home's waste system?

options.A: To allow solids to settle and liquids to flow out to a drain field
options.B: To store rainwater for washing clothes and watering gardens
options.C: To incinerate solid waste using high-voltage electric heating
options.D: To pump treated drinking water directly back into household taps

explanation: Think of a septic tank as a settling room: heavy solids sink to the bottom, while the liquid wastewater flows out gently into the underground drain field for natural filtering.

question: Why should nurse researchers avoid using 3D visual effects on bar charts?

options.A: They take up less memory on hospital computers
options.B: They prevent the X-axis from showing words
options.C: They automatically turn the data into a pie chart
options.D: They can distort the bar heights and mislead the reader

explanation: Three-dimensional designs look fancy, but they create optical illusions that make it hard to read the true values. Keep it flat and clear!

question: What does consumer purchasing power refer to?

options.A: The physical strength of shoppers carrying heavy bags from the market
options.B: The financial ability of a household to buy goods and services with their income
options.C: The political influence grocery store chains have over food pricing laws
options.D: The total amount of food a farmer can produce in a single season

explanation: Purchasing power measures what an individual or family can actually afford to buy with available funds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: Which of these is a main goal of doing passive range of motion?

options.A: Increasing active muscle strength
options.B: Lowering high blood pressure instantly
options.C: Keeping joint flexibility and movement
options.D: Treating underlying bone infections

explanation: Well done! Passive movements are specifically designed to keep joints flexible when a patient cannot move themselves.

question: What is needed to make sure digital gadgets and tech actually help student learning?

options.A: Good teacher training and reliable school infrastructure
options.B: Making students wear VR headsets for every single class
options.C: Throwing away all printed nursing textbooks
options.D: Restricting computer use only to top school admin staff

explanation: Tech is only helpful if your school has steady power, working equipment, and teachers who know how to use it with you.

question: What is the main job of a supercomputer in medical research?

options.A: Displaying continuous bedside vital sign waveforms
options.B: Printing hospital administrative billing invoices
options.C: Running daily electronic charting for individual patient rooms
options.D: Performing complex calculations for research like genomic sequencing

explanation: Spot on! Supercomputers are extreme number-crunchers used for massive scientific breakthroughs like decoding human genes.

question: A community health nurse notices three children from the same compound presenting with watery diarrhea and vomiting. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Treat the patients, stabilize them, and report the suspected cholera cases to local authorities
options.B: Close down the entire primary health care clinic until next week
options.C: Tell the parents to stay home and wait to see if the symptoms go away on their own
options.D: Send a formal letter to an international health organization via postal mail

explanation: Great nursing care means treating the patient right in front of you while also sounding the alarm to protect the whole community from a potential outbreak.

question: When handling medical errors openly, what does the acronym CAR stand for?

options.A: Communication, Apology, and Resolution
options.B: Clinical Accountability Review
options.C: Careful Assessment and Recovery
options.D: Clinical Adverse Response

explanation: CAR stands for Communication, Apology, and Resolution. It is a helpful framework we use to address medical mistakes openly and honestly with patients and their families.

question: Why must a triage nurse keep monitoring patients who are waiting in the emergency queue?

options.A: Doctors refuse to see patients without updated charts
options.B: Waiting patients often complain about the slow service
options.C: A stable patient's condition can suddenly get worse
options.D: Hospital policy requires a vital sign check every five minutes

explanation: Illness can change quickly! Someone who looks stable at first triage can crash suddenly and need immediate help. Keep a close eye on your patients.

question: What is osteomyelitis?

options.A: An autoimmune destruction of bone lining
options.B: A malignant tumor originating in the marrow
options.C: A degenerative softening of the cartilage joints
options.D: An infection of the bone and bone marrow

explanation: Osteomyelitis is simply an infection that gets inside the bone and its inner marrow. You've got this!

question: How can mechanical ventilation affect a patient's blood circulation?

options.A: It has no effect on heart function
options.B: It increases the heart rate in every patient
options.C: It permanently damages heart muscle fibers
options.D: It alters chest pressures, which can impact blood flow

explanation: Because the machine pushes air into the chest using positive pressure, it changes the normal pressures inside. This can sometimes make it a bit harder for blood to return to the heart. Good to keep in mind at the bedside!

question: What is the special thing about a "community of solution"?

options.A: Its members interact exclusively through mobile phone apps
options.B: It forms around a specific problem or shared health goal
options.C: It exists permanently within a single government district
options.D: It is defined strictly by natural rivers and mountains

explanation: Nice one! These groups team up specifically to tackle and solve a particular issue or health challenge together.

question: How do long-term high food prices contribute to chronic illnesses like diabetes and obesity in vulnerable communities?

options.A: By eliminating the body's natural ability to process natural sugars
options.B: By forcing families to rely heavily on cheap, highly processed, carbohydrate-heavy foods
options.C: By providing extra financial funds for families to buy excessive amounts of meat
options.D: By encouraging children to exercise less due to high grocery store bills

explanation: When healthy food becomes too expensive, families buy cheap processed items that lack nutrition and promote chronic disease. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h8)

question: Which of these is a classic 'high-touch' surface in a hospital ward that needs regular wiping?

options.A: Bedside call button
options.B: Upper wall corner
options.C: Ceiling ventilation tiles
options.D: Hospital room floor

explanation: Call buttons, door handles, and bed rails are touched by everyone all day long, making them high-touch hotspots for germs.

question: What is the main purpose of a clean delivery kit in community health?

options.A: To reduce infection risks during childbirth
options.B: To replace the need for skilled birth attendants
options.C: To speed up the second stage of labor
options.D: To diagnose high-risk pregnancies early

explanation: Delivery kits provide sterile or clean barriers and tools that prevent harmful bacteria from entering the birth canal or umbilical cord, lowering infection rates. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which type of validity involves checking if a new tool compares well with an established gold standard?

options.A: Surface validity
options.B: Criterion validity
options.C: Face validity
options.D: Content validity

explanation: Criterion validity is established when a new instrument scores similarly to a trusted, proven gold-standard tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h6)

question: What is the main consequence of damaged intestinal villi on a patient's nutrition?

options.A: The liver stops making bile needed for breaking down sugars.
options.B: The stomach starts producing too much acid for digestion.
options.C: Reduced surface area leads to poor absorption of essential nutrients.
options.D: Food moves backward into the esophagus causing frequent vomiting.

explanation: Intestinal villi are responsible for absorbing digested nutrients into the bloodstream; when they are damaged, nutrient uptake fails. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h4)

question: Where do we usually find the stubborn bacteria spores that cause tetanus?

options.A: Purified bottled water
options.B: Soil
options.C: Clean indoor air
options.D: Fresh pasteurized milk

explanation: Tetanus spores love hanging out in the dirt and soil, waiting for a little cut or scrape to sneak into the body.

question: Which level of prevention involves giving childhood immunizations to stop disease before it starts?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Primary prevention aims to prevent disease or injury before it ever occurs through measures like immunizations and health education. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h3)

question: During a virtual visit, what is one of the main things a tele-nurse does?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations
options.B: Triage and symptom assessment
options.C: Manufacturing medical devices
options.D: Operating hospital financial accounts

explanation: Tele-nurses spend a lot of time listening to patient complaints, checking symptoms, and figuring out how urgently they need care.

question: What is the main job of the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical brain circuit in OCD?

options.A: Controlling voluntary muscle movement in the upper extremities
options.B: Producing visual images during rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Filtering sensory information and regulating behavioral habits
options.D: Regulating body temperature and fluid balance in the kidneys

explanation: You nailed it! When this pathway has trouble filtering routine signals, the brain gets stuck in repetitive loops of thoughts and actions.

question: Why does the body slow down its metabolism during long periods of starvation?

options.A: To conserve remaining energy stores and prolong survival
options.B: To build up extra muscle tissue in the limbs
options.C: To prepare the digestive tract for a heavy meal
options.D: To increase physical activity levels automatically

explanation: It is a brilliant survival mechanism. When food is scarce, the body dials down its energy use so it doesn't burn through its fat and muscle too fast.

question: Why do many hyperthyroid patients in low-resource settings often arrive at the hospital with very advanced illness?

options.A: Delays in reaching specialized care and initial use of traditional remedies
options.B: Widespread mandatory fortification of local staple foods with thyroxine
options.C: Genetic mutations that make local strains of the disease grow faster
options.D: Strict government bans on importing standard antithyroid medicines

explanation: Long distances to health facilities and trying local herbal remedies first often mean patients only reach the hospital when their illness is quite advanced.

question: You check a patient's lab results, like serum albumin and electrolytes. What type of nutritional data is this?

options.A: Environmental data
options.B: Anthropometric data
options.C: Dietary history
options.D: Biochemical data

explanation: Spot on! Lab tests and blood markers give you biochemical data, showing what is happening inside the patient's body chemically.

question: A toddler is brought to the clinic with sunken eyes, fussiness, and drinks the ORS eagerly. How would you classify this dehydration?

options.A: Chronic malnutrition
options.B: Severe dehydration
options.C: Some dehydration
options.D: No dehydration

explanation: You got it! Irritability, sunken eyes, and drinking eagerly are classic signs of moderate ('some') dehydration. Giving ORS right here in the clinic will help them bounce back.

question: Which of these is a common physical danger resulting from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Rapid fetal bone growth
options.C: Uterine perforation and severe infection
options.D: Permanent high blood pressure

explanation: Correct! When procedures are done without proper training or sterile tools, it can easily tear the uterus and cause severe, life-threatening pelvic infections.

question: How does artificial intelligence help out in advanced EMR systems?

options.A: Setting the room temperature based on patient preference
options.B: Automatically writing hospital discharge summaries without human review
options.C: Replacing the head nurse with a computerized management algorithm
options.D: Analyzing vital sign trends to help predict complications like sepsis early

explanation: Smart algorithms scan patient data behind the scenes to warn the care team of subtle signs of danger before things get critical.

question: What goes on inside the body during the incubation period of an infection?

options.A: The patient experiences severe, disease-specific symptoms
options.B: The body completely eliminates the infectious agent
options.C: The host is fully recovered and no longer contagious
options.D: The pathogen multiplies inside the host before symptoms appear

explanation: Well done! The incubation period is that quiet window of time between catching the germ and first feeling sick.

question: What defines an orphan drug?

options.A: A medication developed to treat a rare medical condition
options.B: An herbal supplement with no scientific research backing
options.C: A controlled substance classified under Schedule I rules
options.D: A drug that has been abandoned by the manufacturing company

explanation: Orphan drugs are specifically created to help patients suffering from rare diseases that affect few people. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h7)

question: A nurse checks lab results for an older adult on a new drug and sees that serum creatinine levels are rising. What does this usually mean?

options.A: Increased gastrointestinal absorption of the oral dose
options.B: Decreased kidney function that may impair drug excretion
options.C: Enhanced liver metabolism clearing the drug too quickly
options.D: Successful antagonism of the drug at the cellular receptor

explanation: Creatinine is a waste product filtered by the kidneys. If it's rising in the blood, it's a red flag that the kidneys are sluggish and struggling to clear out medications properly.

question: What is a common myth people believe about using digital tools in nursing practice?

options.A: People believe computers can completely replace all doctors and nurses.
options.B: People think digital materials can only be used by illiterate community members.
options.C: People assume mobile phones do not require any battery power to operate.
options.D: People believe digital tools completely replace traditional face-to-face nursing contact.

explanation: Digital tools are awesome helpers, but they can never replace the warmth and trust of real human touch and face-to-face nursing care.

question: A patient asks if fresh eggs and plain milk are okay on a gluten-free diet. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only if they are labeled with a special certification stamp.
options.B: Dairy is allowed, but eggs must be strictly avoided.
options.C: Yes, fresh eggs and plain dairy are naturally free of gluten.
options.D: No, all animal products contain traces of wheat protein.

explanation: Pure, unprocessed whole foods like eggs, meat, and plain milk do not contain gluten naturally. Simple and safe!

question: Why must vaccine and medication storage refrigerators have their temperatures checked and recorded regularly?

options.A: To ensure the refrigerator door is locked at all times
options.B: To check if the electricity bill is too high for the ward
options.C: To make sure improper heat does not ruin drug potency
options.D: To calculate how many patients received injections that day

explanation: Many pharmaceutical products degrade quickly if temperatures fluctuate outside the safe cold chain range. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T19#GNS122_U3_T19_h5)

question: Which breath sound is described as a continuous musical whistle heard when airways are narrowed?

options.A: Crackles
options.B: Wheezes
options.C: Rhonchi
options.D: Stridor

explanation: Wheezes are high-pitched musical sounds created when air flows through constricted bronchial tubes. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the main difference between an 'output' and an 'outcome' in advocacy?

options.A: Outputs measure financial costs, while outcomes measure staff attendance
options.B: Outputs happen after the project, while outcomes happen before the project
options.C: Outputs measure activities done, while outcomes measure actual results achieved
options.D: Outputs are qualitative stories, while outcomes are strictly numerical charts

explanation: Think of outputs as what you *did* (like handing out 100 flyers), and outcomes as the actual *change* that happened because of it (like more people getting vaccinated).

question: Where do adult Ascaris worms love to live inside the human body?

options.A: The small intestine
options.B: The bloodstream
options.C: The large intestine
options.D: The liver and bile ducts

explanation: Adult roundworms settle comfortably in the small intestine, where they hang out, feed, and lay eggs.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical duty of a nurse working in a community mental health center?

options.A: Administering long-acting injectable psychiatric medications
options.B: Performing major neurosurgery for treatment-resistant depression
options.C: Connecting vulnerable clients with local housing and food resources
options.D: Providing psychoeducation to patients and their family members

explanation: Nurses in community settings do not perform neurosurgery; their role focuses on support, education, medication management, and resource linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the basic working unit of the human kidney?

options.A: The nephron
options.B: The loop of Henle
options.C: The renal pelvis
options.D: The ureter

explanation: Great job! The nephron is the tiny but mighty unit inside your kidneys that filters your blood and makes urine. You've got this!

question: You notice a yellow infectious waste bag is overflowing on your treatment trolley. What should you do?

options.A: Leave the bag open until the end of the shift for the cleaning crew
options.B: Tie the bag securely and replace it with a new one without pressing the contents down
options.C: Press the waste down firmly with both hands to make room for more items
options.D: Transfer some of the infectious waste into the general office dustbin

explanation: Never push down on a waste bag with your hands! Hidden needles or sharp bits can easily pierce the bag and give you a severe injury.

question: A midwife is reviewing a case where an embryo has successfully burrowed beneath the surface lining of the uterus. Which stage of implantation is this?

options.A: Cleavage
options.B: Invasion
options.C: Apposition
options.D: Adhesion

explanation: Brilliant! When the cells actively dig through the surface and sink into the womb lining, we call it invasion.

question: What dietary advice is most appropriate for a nurse to give a patient managing Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: Eliminate all forms of carbohydrates completely from the diet
options.B: Rely entirely on fruit juices for daily hydration and energy
options.C: Choose high-fiber foods and practice moderate portion control
options.D: Eat only once a day to keep blood sugar levels completely flat

explanation: Balanced nutrition focuses on whole grains, fiber, and sensible portions rather than dangerous elimination diets. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: How does an overly competitive and hostile classroom climate affect students?

options.A: It speeds up the mastery of human anatomy
options.B: It breeds stress and fear of asking questions
options.C: It removes all forms of academic anxiety
options.D: It encourages open sharing of clinical techniques

explanation: Hostile environments make students terrified of looking foolish, which stops them from asking the vital questions they need to learn.

question: When setting up a temporary camp for people displaced by a disaster, which type of location should you strictly avoid?

options.A: Flat land with easy access to roads
options.B: Areas far away from stagnant water bodies
options.C: Locations with proper ventilation and spacing
options.D: Flood-prone zones and landslide-risk areas

explanation: Putting a camp in a swampy or flood-prone area just invites another disaster. Always look for high, safe ground!

question: Which of the following actions is NOT appropriate when a nurse discovers a severely irregular pulse in a resting patient?

options.A: Notify the attending physician promptly about the irregular rhythm
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.C: Review the medication record for heart-altering drugs
options.D: Assess the patient for dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath

explanation: Waiting to report an acute abnormal finding puts the patient at risk; abnormal signs require prompt assessment and notification. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why is a one-time training workshop at the start of a project not enough for long-term success?

options.A: New staff constantly join the ward and need to learn the protocols too
options.B: Hospital rules forbid nurses from attending more than one workshop
options.C: Initial workshops never cover the correct clinical procedures
options.D: Staff members forget everything they learned within the first hour

explanation: High staff turnover means continuous, ongoing education is essential so new arrivals understand and follow established practices. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h5)

question: What do we call a sudden poisoning that happens right after a person has one large exposure to a chemical?

options.A: Acute exposure
options.B: Chronic exposure
options.C: Dermal accumulation
options.D: Systemic absorption

explanation: You've got this! Acute exposure simply means a one-time, short contact with a substance that quickly leads to symptoms or harm. Think of it as a sudden event, unlike chronic exposure which builds up over a long time.

question: When documenting injuries resulting from suspected gender-based violence in the patient's medical record, what is the best practice for a nurse to follow?

options.A: Omit any mention of violence to protect the privacy of the family
options.B: Write down personal opinions about who started the argument in the home
options.C: Describe the injuries vaguely to avoid getting involved in police investigations
options.D: Record exact quotes from the patient and use objective descriptions of physical findings

explanation: Accurate, objective documentation using direct quotes and precise physical descriptions is crucial for both clinical continuity and potential legal proceedings. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h7)

question: What is another common medical name for the subcutaneous tissue layer?

options.A: Hypodermis
options.B: Epidermis
options.C: Fascia
options.D: Periosteum

explanation: You got it! 'Hypo' means beneath and 'dermis' refers to the skin, so hypodermis is just another name for the subcutaneous layer right underneath.

question: How does involving the community help improve disaster outcomes?

options.A: It stops people from talking about past traumatic events
options.B: It empowers residents to act effectively and heed early warnings
options.C: It removes the responsibility of government agencies entirely
options.D: It ensures that disasters never happen in rural settlements

explanation: Informed communities stay calm and react faster, which saves many lives during those critical first minutes of an emergency. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h6)

question: A weak patient is learning to walk down the hallway and needs a little extra support to stay steady. What should you use?

options.A: A mechanical hoist
options.B: A slide sheet
options.C: A ceiling lift
options.D: A gait belt

explanation: You're doing great! A gait belt goes snugly around the patient's waist, giving you a safe and secure grip to steady them as they walk.

question: What should a patient do right after coughing into a disposable tissue?

options.A: Place the tissue in their pocket for later use
options.B: Leave the tissue on the bedside table
options.C: Hand the tissue directly to the attending nurse
options.D: Throw the tissue in the trash and clean their hands

explanation: Correct! Tossing the tissue straight into the bin and cleaning up stops those sneaky germs from spreading to bed tables or other people.

question: Why do nurse researchers use experimental designs instead of simple observation?

options.A: Observation cannot control outside factors that might skew results
options.B: Experiments are much easier to perform on busy wards
options.C: Patients prefer being in experimental groups
options.D: Observation takes too much money and time

explanation: Active control in experiments lets researchers rule out other explanations for patient recovery or change, giving much stronger proof than just watching patients. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main role of multimodal sensory association areas?

options.A: To store permanent language dictionaries in the brainstem
options.B: To combine inputs from multiple senses into a single experience
options.C: To send initial motor commands directly to skeletal muscles
options.D: To generate raw electrical impulses in the sensory organs

explanation: Multimodal areas act like a mixing desk, taking separate clues from what you see, touch, smell, and hear and blending them into one complete picture of your environment.

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward
options.B: Purchasing heavy-duty earthquake-resistant generators
options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

explanation: That's right! Laws and policies are non-structural measures that guide us away from dangerous areas without physical building changes.

question: Which natural hazard displaces thousands of people every year in Nigerian coastal and river areas?

options.A: Tidal tsunamis
options.B: Seasonal flooding
options.C: Volcanic eruptions
options.D: Severe blizzards

explanation: Exactly! Heavy seasonal rains often overflow river banks, causing widespread displacement in many parts of Nigeria.

question: A hospital is introducing a new electronic health record system. Who is most likely responsible for training the bedside nursing staff on how to use it?

options.A: The head pharmacist
options.B: The biomedical equipment technician
options.C: The hospital chief executive officer
options.D: The nursing informaticist

explanation: Training staff on new clinical documentation systems falls directly under the educational and implementation duties of a nursing informaticist. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT an environmental barrier to communication?

options.A: Severe patient anxiety and panic
options.B: Distracting television volume
options.C: Loud monitor alarms and busy hallways
options.D: Lack of privacy in a crowded ward

explanation: You got it! Anxiety is an emotional or internal feeling, whereas environmental barriers are about physical surroundings like noise and crowds.

question: Why is careless handling of needles and blades such a big deal in the hospital?

options.A: It damages expensive hospital instruments quickly
options.B: It causes patients to lose trust in the nursing staff
options.C: It can transmit dangerous infections to anyone nearby
options.D: It leads to immediate disciplinary action by management

explanation: A used sharp can easily pass germs straight into the bloodstream through a break in the skin. Always handle with care!

question: Why can severe physical stress or a sudden infection cause a high fasting blood sugar reading?

options.A: Infection causes the kidneys to stop filtering sugar out of the blood.
options.B: Dehydration turns blood cells into pure glucose molecules.
options.C: Fever completely destroys insulin molecules stored in the pancreas.
